display.purpose: Page h1: the centred hero headline (max 16ch) and left-set page and study questions.

headline.purpose: Long study questions that would wrap past three lines at display size.

title.purpose: Section h2s: The short answer, Want to know more?, Have a question?

answer.purpose: The one-paragraph short answer inside the answer card; 1.15rem on phones.

lead.purpose: The hero line under the headline in ink-2, max 46ch; page intros use 1.1rem.

body.purpose: Fold content and prose at 62 to 66ch; 17px under 640px.

control.purpose: Button text. Nav links and chips use 500 at about 0.98rem, stepping to 600 when selected.

small.purpose: Secondary reading lines: the verdict's one-line why, study facts, key-value lists, question chips, link rows and the Saved button.

caption.purpose: Hints, footer, dates, tooltip text and raw registry text.

label.purpose: Verdict labels. Ladder rungs use 0.82rem, 700 on the current rung.

shadows.name: rest-lift
shadows.purpose: Default lift for white surfaces on the sky-white ground: study cards, answer card, search field, news items, open folds. CSS token --shadow.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Study cards on hover, paired with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: Closed accordion items, Q&A entries and ghost buttons: flat with an edge.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: The Saved drawer, over a rgba(31,43,56,.22) scrim.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.value: outline: 3px solid color-mix(in srgb, #2F5BD3 45%, transparent); outline-offset: 2px
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on every interactive element.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Background, border and colour changes on buttons and chips.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Card lift (0.2s) and accordion chevron rotation (0.25s).

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: Inline loading spinner while ClinicalTrials.gov is queried.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables all animation and transition

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Single breakpoint: 17px body, 16px gutter, stacked search, 2 by 2 ladder, icon-only Saved, brand word hidden.

components.html:
The short answer

Yes. After about a year and a half, people on the highest dose lost about 21% of their body weight on average.

Proven and approved

Tested in a large study, checked by outside experts, and approved by the FDA.

  1. Results not in yet
  2. Promising, not checked yet
  3. Shown to work
  4. Proven and approved
components.css: .ds-verdict{font-family:var(--font, Figtree, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;font-size:.88rem;font-weight:600;padding:4px 12px 4px 9px;border-radius:999px;white-space:nowrap;line-height:1.6}.ds-verdict svg{width:15px;height:15px}.ds-v-proven{background:var(--proven-bg);color:var(--proven)}.ds-v-works{background:var(--works-bg);color:var(--works)}.ds-v-promising{background:var(--promising-bg);color:var(--promising)}.ds-v-early{background:var(--early-bg);color:var(--early)}.ds-v-stopped{background:var(--stopped-bg);color:var(--stopped)}.ds-answer{font-family:var(--font, Figtree, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif);background:var(--surface);border-radius:24px;box-shadow:var(--shadow, 0 1px 2px rgba(31,43,56,.04), 0 6px 20px rgba(31,43,56,.06));padding:32px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:18px;max-width:760px;color:var(--ink)}.ds-answer h2{margin:0;font-size:1.4rem;line-height:1.25;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.02em}.ds-big{margin:0;font-size:1.32rem;line-height:1.5;font-weight:500}.ds-sure{display:flex;gap:12px;align-items:flex-start;flex-wrap:wrap;padding-top:18px;border-top:1px solid var(--line-2)}.ds-sure p{margin:0;flex:1;min-width:220px;font-size:.95rem;color:var(--ink-2)}.ds-ladder{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:6px;font-size:.82rem;color:var(--ink-3);text-align:center}.ds-ladder li{padding:8px 6px;border-radius:10px;background:var(--line-2);line-height:1.3;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center}.ds-ladder li.on{font-weight:700;background:var(--proven-bg);color:var(--proven)}

narrative.overview:
TrialSignal reads like a good patient leaflet set on a calm screen: an everyday question, a short plain answer, one label that says how sure we can be, and everything else folded away until asked for. The ground is an airy sky-white, content sits on soft white rounded surfaces, ink is a soft navy rather than black, and a single friendly blue marks what you can press. The only other colour on the page belongs to the verdict labels, so colour always carries meaning.

Density is deliberately low. One reading column, generous gaps between sections (64px), large body type (18px) and pill-shaped controls with 44 to 48px targets. Depth is soft and ambient: white surfaces lift off the ground with a faint navy-tinted shadow, never a hard edge. Figtree, a friendly geometric sans, does every job from the hero headline to the smallest caption, with weight rather than a second family carrying hierarchy.

This is a single light theme by deliberate choice. The user found the previous slate design too dark; there is no dark mode and none should be added without a new decision. The research-database look (tables of codes, phase jargon, dense grids) is the confirmed anti-reference: codes and key-value lists exist only inside the last "Study details for the curious" fold. The build extends the direction contract's four verdict labels with a fifth, plum "Didn't work or stopped", used in News.
keyCharacteristics: Sky-white ground (`bg`), white rounded surfaces, soft navy ink.
One action blue; four ladder verdicts plus a "stopped" tone are the only other hues.
Every verdict is a pale tint with same-hue deep text and a line icon, always with its words.
Figtree only, 400 to 700, sentence case throughout.
Pills for everything you press, 16 to 24px rounded rectangles for everything you read.
Answer first; details open one at a time.

rules.name: The Blue Means Press Rule
rules.body: The blue family appears only on things that act: buttons, links, the current nav item, selected topics and the icons inside pressable chips and accordion summaries. Never use it for decoration, headings or status.

rules.name: The Verdict Owns Its Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, teal, amber, slate and plum mean "how sure we can be" and nothing else. They never colour a button state, an alert, a chart or a decoration.

rules.name: The Tint and Ink Rule
rules.body: A verdict is always a pale wash with same-hue deep text and a line icon, always with its words. Never a solid fill, never colour alone.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Figtree carries every role. Add weight, not a second typeface.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every heading, button, chip and label is sentence case at normal tracking. No uppercase, no letter-spaced labels, no small caps.

rules.name: The One Column for Reading Rule
rules.body: Anything meant to be read sits in a single column no wider than 760px. Grids are for choosing a study, never for reading one.

rules.name: The Open Lifts Rule
rules.body: A closed fold is flat with a hairline; an open fold lifts with the rest shadow. Depth signals "this is the one you are reading".

dos: **Do** keep the page light: `bg` ground, `surface` cards, `ink` text. This is a single light theme.
**Do** reserve the blue family for things that act, and the verdict tones for "how sure".
**Do** show a verdict label, with its words, wherever a finding appears.
**Do** lead every study with the answer card, then fold the rest into one-at-a-time accordion items.
**Do** use full pills (999px) for controls and 16px or 24px rounded rectangles for reading surfaces.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or more and buttons at 48px.
**Do** keep reading columns at 760px or narrower and prose at 62 to 66ch.
**Do** keep the IRB verification statement visible in the footer on every view.
donts: **Don't** add a dark mode or a dark-ground section; the light, calm ground is a user decision.
**Don't** introduce a second accent colour or use a verdict tone for a button state, alert or decoration.
**Don't** add uppercase eyebrows, kickers or letter-spaced labels; everything is sentence case.
**Don't** add illustrations, mascots, gradients or loud colour.
**Don't** show registry codes, phase numbers or key-value tables in the first layer; they live inside "Study details for the curious".
**Don't** use hard or offset shadows; depth is the soft navy-tinted lift only.
**Don't** mix icon families or fill icons; line icons, stroke 1.8, round caps.
